result.title: Which Loans, Not How Many: Exactly Level-Invariant, Anytime-Valid Monitoring of Deployed Risk Models
result.summary: A refinancing wave can change the number of mortgage prepayments without changing the relationship between scores and prepayment. In a logistic model, conditioning on the monthly count removes the intercept from the likelihood of which loans prepay. Our fixed-start slope product tests a lower bound on the calibration slope. At threshold 20 its probability of ever crossing under the null is at most 5%. The restarted level sum tracks departures from intercept tolerance. A confidence sequence estimates a constant slope, and the restart-intersection rule detects changes in that slope. A continuous mixture avoids the off-grid width floor of a discrete prior. On Freddie Mac loans, fixed-slope resampling reproduces 78% of maintained-model monthly AUC variance in development and 70% in the holdout (95% intervals 57-100% and 48-100%). From fresh holdout starts, the restarted level sum crosses on both paths, and the fixed-start slope product stays below threshold on both. The restart-intersection rule signals a downward change for the frozen model in April 2018 and an upward change for the maintained model in a supplementary run in August 2019.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对已部署的信贷风险模型，提出与每月贷款笔数无关的序列监测方法：用固定起点斜率乘积检验校准斜率下界、用重启水平统计追踪截距偏离、用置信序列与重启交集规则检测参数变化，并在 Freddie Mac 数据上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其 anytime-valid 序列检验与「重启—交集」停止规则，或可为 LVR 中证据累积与何时停止/何时报告漂移的评价提供形式化工具，但该联系较远，能否用于 latent 状态监测需进一步核查。
